_about: Multi-speaker story scenes (Oct 21 story-content brief). Read by StoryScenes (core/data/story_scenes.gd), played by StoryScenePlayer. Each step: [speaker, line, line...]; speaker = an NPC id (portrait + plate), NPC-PLAYER for the Wanderer, "" for narration, or "@set" followed by flags to set at that point. once_flag: skipped once set, set when played. sets: more flags set when played. Voice: docs/design/voice_bible.md.

steps: A barricade of stacked weight plates, painted regulation red. Behind it, a ferret in a pinstriped suit is timing a guard's push-ups with a silver stopwatch.
NPC-QUOTA
Forty-one. Forty-two. Stop. Eleven percent slower than yesterday. We will discuss it at your review.
And you. You walked in at a pace of seven out of ten. Disappointing. But measurable.
NPC-PLAYER
Who are you?
NPC-QUOTA
Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency. I designed the wheels, the schedules and the prison downstairs. The Chancellor does the shouting. I do the arithmetic.
Hold still. I'm measuring you. Grip: low. Stride: uneven. Resolve... unusually high. That is an inefficiency. Let's remove it.
NPC-QUOTA
Ninety-four seconds. You beat me in ninety-four seconds.
I will note it. I note everything. The Chancellor will not enjoy this figure.
She clicks the stopwatch, steps through a side door marked for staff only, and is gone before the guard finishes his push-up.
On the arm of the Throne of Gains someone has left a schedule, timed to the second, and a silver stopwatch, still running.
NPC-FLEX
Quota's gone. Left for the Capital before the dust settled. She always did leave early.
We'll keep the schedule. It will make good kindling. Breathe, son. Nobody here is on the clock any more.
By the last energy wheel, a ferret in pinstripes is timing Rollo's crews. The crews are lying in the sun. She is still timing them.
NPC-QUOTA
You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and eleven minutes. I have had the figure framed.
These wheels lit the facade at a hundred and ten percent. Now they are 'resting'. Do you know what rest is? Unmeasured time.
NPC-PLAYER
They're allowed to stop.
NPC-QUOTA
Nobody is allowed anything. People are scheduled. Let me schedule you.
NPC-QUOTA
Eighty-one seconds. Faster than last time. You have improved by fourteen percent.
That was not a compliment. I simply cannot leave a figure unsaid.
NPC-ROLLO
Flex wants someone... to run the new break schedule... up in the Gainlands. Someone who can count.
NPC-QUOTA
Breaks. Scheduled breaks. Mandatory rest, for everyone, forever.
I will hate every minute. I will time every one.
She sits down on the edge of the wheel, stopwatch in her lap, and for the first time in ten years she does not click it.
The Prototype Bay smells of hot iron and burnt sugar. A war machine squats on a pallet: half oven, half cannon, one wheel still in its packing straw.
NPC-CRUMB
Inspection! ATTEN-TION! Who put a dent in my souffle cannon? Battle stations! This is not a drill, it is a souffle!
NPC-CRUMB
And what is THIS? A civilian. In my bay. Unsupervised. With flavour on his breath.
Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense. Taste is a weakness, son. Paste is a strategy.
NPC-CRUMB
Whisk formation! Field-test the prototype on the intruder. I have a ration meeting.
He salutes the machine. The machine salutes back with a ladle. The Colonel marches out before it has finished preheating.
The war machine sags and steams. Taped to its side is an inspection card under a seal of crossed forks: PASSED. NEEDS MORE SALT. - COL. C. CRUMB.
NPC-BASIL
The Colonel's gone. His office is empty. He took the paste recipe with him.
It's one word long. The word is 'paste'.
NPC-ESCOFFINA
He left before dessert. He always did. They say he's feeding the whole Capital now, from a factory.
Grey, from a tap. Somebody ought to teach that man to cook.
At the end of the Vat Floor, behind a door with a hatch for rations, is a kitchen. A real one. Copper pans, a cold stove, and a badger in a medal-covered chef's coat guarding a locked pantry.
NPC-CRUMB
HALT! This is a restricted pantry! Those recipes are confiscated for the war effort!
What war? The war on FLAVOUR, son. Every citizen fed the same, at the same time, from the same tap. Perfect discipline.
NPC-PLAYER
Marlo says you can't taste it either.
NPC-CRUMB
Taste is a weakness. Whisk formation! Golems, to the vats! Nobody touches my pantry!
NPC-CRUMB
Stand down. Stand DOWN. I said... oh, everyone's already lying down. Very well.
The pantry door swings open. Shelves of confiscated jars: pickles, jams, a wheel of cheese with a ration number on it. Somewhere a vat coughs and stops.
NPC-CRUMB
I invented the paste because nobody could get it wrong. You can't burn paste. You can't oversalt it.
You can't... taste it. I never could, you know. Not since the war that wasn't.
NPC-MARLO
Then you'll learn. The Grand Chef is taking students. She starts everyone the same way: first, water.
NPC-CRUMB
...Yes, Chef.
The mill wheel is gripped by roots as thick as a cart. Someone has been trimming them. Very neatly. Into the shape of a smiling man in a circlet.
NPC-CLIPWELL
Mind the topiary, dear. That's His Perfection from the left. The right side is still growing in.
NPC-CLIPWELL
Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper. I outlawed composting. So untidy. All that rot, lying about in heaps, being honest.
NPC-PLAYER
Nothing rots here any more.
NPC-CLIPWELL
Isn't it lovely? I brought the Archdruid a little seed, a gift. Life that never ends. She was so very sad, and now nothing ever has to go.
And now, dear, I'm afraid I have a weed to remove.
NPC-CLIPWELL
Well. You've made a dreadful mess of my hedges. I shall send a note.
She opens a wide green umbrella, steps neatly over the roots and walks away up the ravine toward the Capital road, not one hair out of place.
NPC-BRAMBLE
The Groundskeeper's gone. Packed her shears and left for the Capital the moment the Archdruid woke.
NPC-BRAMBLE
She left one pair behind, in a compost heap. Granny Gristle is keeping them. 'Found, not stolen,' she says. Twice.
Beside the Sick Patch, a hare in groundskeeper green is measuring Old Fern's seedling with a ruler. It is an inch over regulation. She has written that down.
NPC-CLIPWELL
Out of regulation. Everything is out of regulation now. The lawns, the hedges. They grow in whatever direction they like.
NPC-FERN
That's what hedges DO.
NPC-CLIPWELL
I gave her the seed because she was crying. I thought, if nothing ever ends, then nobody ever has to cry again.
That's tidy, isn't it? Isn't that tidy?
NPC-PLAYER
Nothing grew there for ten years.
NPC-FERN
Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump. Peel from shell. Messy work.
NPC-CLIPWELL
...I shall bring my own gloves.
A peacock in a lavender coat sweeps across the lobby with a ribbon, a pair of golden scissors and a speaking trumpet.
NPC-PLUME
Great news, citizens! The D.N.A. has been freed, a change His Perfection fully supports and in fact arranged!
And you must be the volunteer. A Certificate of Participation. Frame it, or don't. It's been notarized either way.
NPC-AGNES
That's Percival Plume, dear. Deputy Minister of Good News. He drafted the transfer. Every page of it.
NPC-PLUME
And filed it on a Tuesday! Must dash. Ribbons to cut, a Capital to reassure. Toodle-oo!
He snips the ribbon, which was holding nothing up, and is gone before Agnes can find the right form.
The castle gate is white and gold and perfectly symmetrical. In its shadow, hood up, stands the woman who pulled you out of the woods, as if she was always going to be here.
NPC-ELOWEN
Don't look so surprised. Somebody has to watch the door while you knock it down.
NPC-PLUME
Great news, citizens! The traitor has been located!
Guards in polished armour pour from the gatehouse. Not toward you. Toward her.
NPC-PLUME
Miss {rescuer_full}, I presume. Former junior Path-ologist. Absent without leave. Removed one item of laboratory property, which has been walking about ever since.
@set
rescuer_named
NPC-PLUME
Don't fret, Miss Vey. Your father is very understanding about these things. Take her home, gentlemen. The long way.
NPC-ELOWEN
Don't follow me, {wanderer}! Get to the top. That's the only way any of this ends.
They are through a side door before you reach it. The door has no handle on this side. Of course it doesn't.
NPC-PLAYER
{rescuer}. Her name is {rescuer}. I never even asked.
The Necrocrat wing's archive is filing from floor to ceiling. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like a peacock, lies a memo, the ink still wet.
MEMO. To: His Perfection. From: P. Plume. Re: the leak in the lab. The junior Path-ologist has been returned to the Path-ology Lab beneath the forest, to her father. Handled. Promotion?
NPC-PLUME
Ah! You found my memo. Isn't it well written? I used the active voice.
Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News. I drafted the transfer of the D.N.A., notarized it, filed it, and read it out on every loudspeaker in the land.
NPC-PLAYER
Where is the Lab?
NPC-PLUME
Beneath the forest where you... oh, I shouldn't have said that. Never mind. Great news: your visit is being declined!
NPC-PLUME
This is a setback. A temporary, fully reversible, not-at-all-my-fault setback.
I'll draft a statement. 'Minister Plume bravely withdrew.' Yes. Bravely.
He withdraws, bravely, at a run. You fold the memo into your pocket. Beneath the forest. Her father.
NPC-ELDER
Sit down, dearie. Word came from the Capital this morning, by way of a pigeon who was very rude about it.
NPC-ELDER
Plume's men took a girl at the castle gate. The one who carried you out of the woods. {rescuer_full}.
I knew that face the day you walked in here. Her father worked in my laboratory, once. I never trusted her for a minute.
NPC-ELDER
I have been wrong about people before. Once. In 1987. It seems I've gone and done it twice.
NPC-PLAYER
Where did they take her?
NPC-ELDER
Back where she came from, I expect. Somewhere with glass walls and no windows. That's a door I can't open. Not yet.
Eat. You'll want your strength for when it opens.
NPC-WREN
We saw them take her at the gate. Four guards and a peacock with a speaking trumpet. We couldn't get close.
NPC-WREN
The Wrinkles are watching every door out of that castle. If they move her again, we'll know.
Her name goes in the true record. Whatever else happens.
The hatch opens on white light and a smell of disinfectant. A staircase of clean steel goes down through the roots of the forest where you woke up.
Everything about this place is familiar in the way a bruise is familiar. Your hands are shaking. You go down anyway.
A white room, three paces by four. Ten years of tally marks on the wall in rows of five, scratched with a spoon handle. Low down, where a child could reach, a drawing in four colors.
Someone is sitting under the drawing with her knees up and her hands bound, as if she has been keeping it company.
NPC-ELOWEN
Took you long enough, Tess.
NPC-PLAYER
Tess?
NPC-ELOWEN
That's what I called you, when we were small and you were too important to be called anything shorter.
They put me in your cell. My father thinks that's educational. With him it is hard to tell.
NPC-ELOWEN
I'll walk behind you. I know every door down here, and which ones scream.
NPC-ELOWEN
Whatever he says in there, he'll say it kindly. That's the worst part. Don't listen to the voice, Tess. Watch the hands.
The only room in the Lab with a rug. On the desk, a journal in a neat, slanted hand. The last entry is ten years old.
"The Minister knelt to the King. I was asked to hold the east door. I held it open. The boy will be safer with us than with sentiment. We will learn so much." - A. Siphon
NPC-ELOWEN
That's his handwriting.
He told me the King died of a fever. He told me you were a patient. I brought you soup.
NPC-PLAYER
Elowen...
NPC-ELOWEN
Don't. Not yet. If you're kind to me now, I won't be able to walk in there.
The only room in the Lab with a rug. On the desk, a journal in a neat, slanted hand. The last entry is ten years old.
"The Minister knelt to the King. I was asked to hold the east door. I held it open. The boy will be safer with us than with sentiment. We will learn so much." - A. Siphon
NPC-PLAYER
Siphon. Her father held the door.
The Extraction Theater: tiered seats of white steel around a single chair. Dr. Ambrose Siphon looks up from a bench of humming glass, neat, polite and not at all surprised.
NPC-SIPHON
Subject 1. And my daughter. Both of you home at once. I shall have to rearrange the schedule.
You have grown. Remarkable. The draining has been very good for your posture.
NPC-ELOWEN
You held the door, Dad. The night they killed the King and Queen. I read it in your own hand.
NPC-SIPHON
I held a door, sweetheart. Doors are held every day. What came through it was the Minister's choice, not mine.
NPC-ELOWEN
You told me he was a patient. I brought him soup. For years.
NPC-SIPHON
And it was very good soup. You were always confused about kindness. It made you a poor scientist and a lovely daughter.
Please, both of you, sit. This will only drain a little.
NPC-ELOWEN
Tess. His Protocols run on switches, and I know where every one is. I'll take one down each turn. You do the rest.
The Extraction Theater: tiered seats of white steel around a single chair. Dr. Ambrose Siphon looks up from a bench of humming glass, neat, polite and not at all surprised.
NPC-SIPHON
Subject 1. You came back to us. You have grown. Remarkable, after so many cycles.
NPC-SIPHON
My daughter is resting in your old room. She is confused, poor thing. She thinks she rescued something.
Assistants come home. Subjects too. Please, sit. This will only drain a little.
The tanks go dark one by one. Siphon sits down among the cables on the floor of his own theater, like a man who has dropped something very small.
NPC-SIPHON
You were never a Subject. Maren said so, and I called it sentiment.
I called a great many things sentiment.
NPC-ELOWEN
Get up, Dad. You're going to Crosspath. Agnes has a form for you, Maren has a great deal to say, and you are going to listen to all of it.
NPC-SIPHON
...Yes. Yes, I suppose I am.
The four colors rise out of the tanks, through the roof and into the forest, where the trees lean toward them like flowers. You do not feel stronger. You feel less alone.
NPC-ELOWEN
My name is {rescuer_full}. Vey was my mother's. I wanted to say it to you properly once, somewhere with a roof.
The tanks go dark one by one. Siphon sits down among the cables on the floor of his own theater, like a man who has dropped something very small.
Footsteps in the corridor behind you, quick and uneven. Somebody has picked the lock of Cell 4 from the inside.
NPC-ELOWEN
Took you long enough, Tess. I got tired of waiting and let myself out.
NPC-ELOWEN
You held the door, Dad. The night they killed the King and Queen. It's in your journal, in your own hand.
NPC-SIPHON
I held a door, sweetheart. What came through it was the Minister's choice.
NPC-ELOWEN
No. It was yours too. Get up. You're going to Crosspath, and you're going to listen to every word Maren says.
NPC-SIPHON
...Yes. I suppose I am.
The four colors rise out of the tanks, through the roof and into the forest, where the trees lean toward them like flowers. You do not feel stronger. You feel less alone.
NPC-ELOWEN
My name is {rescuer_full}. Vey was my mother's. I wanted to say it to you properly once, somewhere with a roof.
Someone is sitting on a rock at the mouth of the Forgotten Cave, hood up, sharpening a pencil with a scalpel.
NPC-ELOWEN
You freed a whole Path. On your own. With a deck you'd known for a week.
Let me see your hands. Steadier. Good. That's the first thing I've been able to tick off in a long time.
NPC-PLAYER
Who are you?
NPC-ELOWEN
Still a friend. Still all I can give you.
I'm not staying in town. The old woman with the shell looks at me like I owe her a pie.
NPC-ELOWEN
Keep going. I'll know when the next one falls. The woods go quiet when a Path comes loose.
The hooded figure is back at the cave mouth with two cups of something hot. She hands you one without asking.
NPC-ELOWEN
Two Paths. People in town are singing again. Badly, but they're singing.
NPC-PLAYER
You knew I'd come back here.
NPC-ELOWEN
You always came back to the same places. Even when you were...
Drink your tea. It's for the shaking.
NPC-PLAYER
Even when I was what?
NPC-ELOWEN
Even when you were someone who couldn't. Ask me something easier.
NPC-PLAYER
Favourite colour?
NPC-ELOWEN
Four of them. Next question.
She is waiting at the cave mouth again with her hood down, as if she forgot it was up. Her eyes are tired and very sure.
NPC-ELOWEN
Three. I used to think you were someone else. Someone I lost when we were kids. Now I'm starting to think...
No. Not until I'm certain. Too many people around here say things before they're certain.
NPC-PLAYER
You knew me. Before.
NPC-ELOWEN
I knew a boy who fell on his behind trying to lift a dumbbell, and who ate the frosting off every layer of his cake.
You'd have liked him. He was terrible at hiding things.
The cave mouth is quiet. This time she is standing, cloak fastened, a satchel of four-coloured vials over her shoulder, ready to go somewhere.
NPC-ELOWEN
All four. The kingdom is breathing again. Like voices through a wall, except the wall is coming down.
There's only the Capital left. Only him.
NPC-PLAYER
Come with me.
NPC-ELOWEN
I'll be at the castle gate when you get there. Somebody has to watch the door while you knock it down.
And when it's over, I'll tell you everything. My name first. I promise.
